questions.question_text: Which of the following atmospheric layers contains the ozone layer that absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer is predominantly located within the stratosphere, roughly 10 to 50 kilometers above Earth's surface.

questions.question_text: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was chosen as the capital compromise between rival cities Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question_text: Which constitutional amendment introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India?
questions.explanation: The Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016 introduced the nationwide GST framework in India.

questions.question_text: Who is known as the 'Iron Man of India'?
questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel earned the title for his crucial role in integrating the princely states into the Indian Union.

questions.question_text: The headquarters of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The ICJ is located at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.question_text: Which of the following mountain ranges separates Europe from Asia?
questions.explanation: The Ural Mountains are traditionally considered the natural geographical boundary between Europe and Asia.

questions.question_text: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi served as India's first and to date only female Prime Minister, holding office starting in 1966.

questions.question_text: The famous ancient monument 'Colosseum' is located in which country?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum is an elliptical amphitheatre located in the center of Rome, Italy.

questions.question_text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Equality before Law?
questions.explanation: Article 14 of the Indian Constitution states that the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws.

questions.question_text: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: The Yen is the official currency of Japan and one of the most traded currencies globally.

questions.question_text: Which planet in our solar system has the most prominent ring system?
questions.explanation: Saturn is famous for its massive and dazzling ring system composed mostly of ice particles and rocky debris.

questions.question_text: Who wrote the famous book 'Discovery of India'?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar fort between 1942 and 1945.

questions.question_text: Which river is the longest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile River is traditionally considered the longest river in the world, flowing northward through Africa.

questions.question_text: Which gas is most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up approximately 78% of Earth's atmosphere by volume.

questions.question_text: Which article of the Constitution of India provides for the establishment of the Finance Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 280 of the Indian Constitution provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission by the President every five years or earlier.

questions.question_text: What is the chemical name of the common baking soda used in households?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is chemically known as sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3).

questions.question_text: Which river is the longest river flowing entirely within the territory of India?
questions.explanation: The Godavari is often referred to as the 'Dakshina Ganga' and is the longest river whose course lies entirely within India.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten served as the first Governor-General of independent India from 1947 to 1948, followed by C. Rajagopalachari as the first Indian Governor-General.

questions.question_text: Which international organization has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland?
options: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
questions.explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO) is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. (UNESCO is in Paris, FAO in Rome, and IMF in Washington, D.C.).

questions.question_text: Which Indian state shares its international border with maximum neighboring countries?
questions.explanation: Sikkim shares borders with three countries: Bhutan, China (Tibet), and Nepal.

questions.question_text: Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'?
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.question_text: Which day is observed globally as 'International Yoga Day'?
questions.explanation: June 21 was declared as International Yoga Day by the United Nations General Assembly in 2014.

questions.question_text: Which National Park in India is famous for being the last refuge of the endangered Asiatic Lion?
questions.explanation: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary in Gujarat is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion.

questions.question_text: The famous monument 'Gateway of India' is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The Gateway of India was built in Mumbai and completed in 1924.

questions.question_text: Which vitamin is essential for blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K plays a crucial role in blood coagulation and preventing excessive bleeding.

questions.question_text: In which year did India adopt its Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constitution of India came into effect on January 26, 1950.

questions.question_text: Which gas constitutes the maximum percentage of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up approximately 78% of the Earth's atmosphere.

questions.question_text: Who wrote the famous ancient Indian treatise on statecraft and economic policy, 'Arthashastra'?
questions.explanation: Chanakya, also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta, authored the Arthashastra during the Maurya Empire.

questions.question_text: Which of the following layers of the Earth's atmosphere is closest to the surface?
questions.explanation: The troposphere is the lowest layer of Earth's atmosphere and contains approximately 75% of the atmosphere's mass.

questions.question_text: What is the chemical symbol for the element Gold?
questions.explanation: The chemical symbol 'Au' is derived from 'aurum', the Latin word for gold.

questions.question_text: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer is a scientific instrument used in meteorology to measure atmospheric pressure.

questions.question_text: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, located in The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.question_text: Which vitamin is primarily synthesized in the human body through exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is often called the 'sunshine vitamin' because it is produced in the skin in response to sunlight.

questions.question_text: Which planet in our solar system is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars is called the Red Planet because of iron oxide (rust) prevalent on its surface.

questions.question_text: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceanic divisions.

questions.question_text: Who painted the famous artwork 'Mona Lisa'?
questions.explanation: The Mona Lisa was painted by the Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci.

questions.question_text: What is the hardest natural substance found on Earth?
questions.explanation: Diamond is an allotrope of carbon where the carbon atoms are arranged in a crystal structure called diamond cubic, making it the hardest known natural material.

questions.question_text: Which gas makes up the majority of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.

questions.question_text: Which animal is known as the 'Ship of the Desert'?
questions.explanation: Camels are called the ship of the desert because they can walk easily on sand and survive long periods without water.

questions.question_text: What is the main component of the sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun is composed primarily of hydrogen (about 73%) and helium (about 25%).

questions.question_text: Which continent is known as the 'Dark Continent'?
questions.explanation: Africa was historically referred to as the 'Dark Continent' because much of the interior was unknown to Europeans.

questions.question_text: What is the freezing point of water in Celsius?
questions.explanation: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius (or 32 degrees Fahrenheit).

questions.question_text: Which of the following international organizations has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland?
questions.explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health, headquartered in Geneva.

questions.question_text: Which element is the most abundant by mass in the Earth's crust?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is the most abundant chemical element in the Earth's crust, making up approximately 46.6% of its mass.

questions.question_text: The famous painting 'Mona Lisa' was created by which Renaissance artist?
questions.explanation: The Mona Lisa is a half-length portrait painting by the Italian artist Leonardo da Vinci, created during the Renaissance.

questions.question_text: What is the longest river in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile River is traditionally accepted as the longest river in the world.

questions.question_text: In which country would you find the ancient ruins of Machu Picchu?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu is an Incan citadel set high in the Andes Mountains in Peru.

questions.question_text: Who proposed the Theory of Relativity?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein developed the theory of relativity, which revolutionized theoretical physics.

questions.question_text: Which desert is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert and the third largest desert overall in the world.

questions.question_text: What is the chemical symbol for Gold?
questions.explanation: Au is the chemical symbol for gold, derived from the Latin word 'aurum'.

questions.question_text: Which ocean is the largest by surface area?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceanic divisions.

questions.question_text: Which instrument is used to measure the total distance traveled by a motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: An odometer tracks the cumulative distance a vehicle has traveled since its manufacture or last reset, whereas a speedometer measures current speed.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of a vehicle's catalytic converter?
options: To convert harmful exhaust pollutants into less harmful emissions
To amplify the sound of the engine exhaust
To generate electrical power for the dashboard
To cool down the transmission fluid
questions.explanation: Catalytic converters use chemical reactions to reduce toxic gases like carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, and nitrogen oxides in vehicle exhaust.

questions.question_text: In the context of road safety, what does 'defensive driving' primarily mean?
options: Driving aggressively to prevent other drivers from cutting in
Anticipating potential hazards and making safe allowances for the errors of others
Traveling below the minimum speed limit on highways
Keeping the windows closed and doors locked at all times
questions.explanation: Defensive driving is a set of driving skills that goes beyond mere rule-following, focusing on accident avoidance through anticipation and caution.

questions.question_text: What does the acronym 'ABS' stand for in automotive engineering?
questions.explanation: ABS is a safety system that prevents the wheels from locking up during braking, thereby maintaining tractive contact with the road surface.

questions.question_text: Why is it dangerous to rest your foot on the clutch pedal while driving at cruising speeds ('riding the clutch')?
options: It causes premature wear on the release bearing and clutch pressure plate
It locks the steering wheel in place
questions.explanation: Resting weight on the clutch pedal creates partial engagement, causing friction and unnecessary wear on internal clutch components.

questions.question_text: Which national highway system connects the four major metropolitan cities of India (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata), forming a highway loop?
questions.explanation: The Golden Quadrilateral is a highway network connecting India's four largest metropolitan areas.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)?
options: Manufacturing commercial transport vehicles and spare parts
Developing, maintaining, and managing national highways across the country
Issuing international driving permits and driver licenses
Regulating retail fuel pricing and petroleum distribution
questions.explanation: NHAI is the nodal agency responsible for the development and maintenance of India's national highway network.

questions.question_text: In the context of vehicle emissions, what does 'Bharat Stage' (BS) emission standards regulate?
options: The physical dimensions and seating capacity of commercial buses
The maximum permissible limits of air pollutants discharged from internal combustion engines
The minimum fuel octane rating required for diesel engines
The sound decibel limits permitted for vehicle horns and sirens
questions.explanation: Bharat Stage emission standards set legal limits for pollutant emissions from motor vehicles in India.

questions.question_text: Which state agency or ministry in India is principally responsible for formulating national transport policies and motor vehicle legislation?
options: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)
Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises
questions.explanation: MoRTH is the apex body responsible for formulating and administering road transport and highway laws in India.

questions.question_text: What does 'FASTag' utilize to enable automatic cashless toll collection on national highways?
options: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) pairing with mobile phones
Optical Character Recognition (OCR) license plate scanning
questions.explanation: FASTag uses RFID technology affixed on the vehicle windscreen to deduct toll fees directly from a prepaid account without stopping.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of a tachometer in a motor vehicle instrument cluster?
options: To measure engine crankshaft speed in revolutions per minute (RPM)
questions.explanation: The tachometer helps drivers choose optimal shift points and prevents engine over-revving.

questions.question_text: What does the term 'aquaplaning' (or hydroplaning) refer to while driving?
options: Driving through a deep river ford
A layer of water building up between the tires and the road surface, causing a loss of traction
Washing the vehicle body with high-pressure water jets
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires cannot channel water away fast enough, causing the vehicle to lift and skate on the water film.

questions.question_text: The author's primary purpose in contrasting centralized governance models with localized policy implementation is to:
options: Criticize the inefficiency of federal institutions, advocating for complete regional autonomy.
Suggest that international bodies must completely oversee all domestic governance decisions.
Argue that optimal policy formulation requires synthesizing top-down planning with ground-level adaptability.
Prove that historical policy failures are solely due to political interference, not structural issues.
questions.explanation: The passage argues that effective governance is achieved not by choosing one model, but by blending high-level strategy with local practical knowledge.
